audit.why: 48.61% over 469 games with a chart of Rumble 2/3 and first item, Skill elsewhere. The prose already frames it as Rumble's lane pre-6 and a teamfight tossup after, which matches both the rate and a kit whose value is engage rather than duelling.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'Zac E up' spike says Elastic Slingshot 'has a long telegraph' with no cooldown, and Let's Bounce is never costed. The packet also flags the matchup for having no cooldown sequencing anywhere.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9 seconds — 21 at rank 1 is the longest single window either champion has in this lane, and the entire mid-lane plan is built on it. Let's Bounce is 120/105/90.
audit.corrected: Give Elastic Slingshot 21 seconds at rank 1 and Let's Bounce 120 seconds, so 'track his E' becomes a countable window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (a) wants.foe[0] has Zac 'chain W CC' — Unstable Matter is not crowd control. Zac's displacement is on Q, E and R. (b) Unstable Matter is never mentioned in the matchup at all, and it is the ability that decides every extended trade: 5-second cooldown, 350 range, damage as a percentage of the target's maximum health. Cell Division is also only ever called 'blob sustain' — the four-bloblet revive on a five-minute cooldown is never stated.
audit.why: Riot's Unstable Matter text: 'Zac explodes outward towards nearby enemies, dealing a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage,' 5s cooldown. Rumble's whole plan is to stand in Flamespitter range (600) and burn him down; Unstable Matter at 350 means every second Rumble stays inside that inner ring costs him max health on a five-second loop. Cell Division: 'Upon taking fatal damage, Zac splits into 4 bloblets... he will revive... This ability has a 5 minute cooldown' — whether it is available changes whether a dive is worth starting.
audit.corrected: Fix the CC attribution to Stretching Strikes, add Unstable Matter's 5s max-health pulse as the reason to burst and leave, and name Cell Division's revive with its five-minute cooldown as a pre-commit check.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (P Cell Division, Q Stretching Strikes, W Unstable Matter)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track Elastic Slingshot' is repeated four times without a single number, so there is nothing to count and no stated punish length.
audit.why: 21 seconds at rank 1 versus Unstable Matter's 5 is the whole shape of the lane: one long window Rumble owns, one short loop Zac owns. Stating both turns posture into a rule.
audit.corrected: Put 21 seconds on Elastic Slingshot and 5 seconds on Unstable Matter in the mid-lane plan.

edits.before: Liandry's Torment makes Flamespitter eat through Zac's HP scaling — his blob sustain cannot keep pace with percent-health burn at this stage.
edits.after: Liandry's burn eats through his HP stack, but Unstable Matter answers in kind — max-health damage every 5 seconds inside 350 range.

edits.before: Elastic Slingshot has a long telegraph — if you misread it and eat it at low HP, Zac chains W and you die before Equalizer can save you.
edits.after: Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1 with a long telegraph — misread it at low HP and the Stretching Strikes chain kills you.

edits.before: Land Elastic Slingshot to skip your Scrap Shield and chain W CC before you can respond with Q
edits.after: Land Elastic Slingshot's knockup and chain Stretching Strikes before you can answer with Q

edits.before: Stack blob passive sustain by letting skirmishes go long so his HP regen offsets Flamespitter tick damage
edits.after: Let skirmishes run long: Unstable Matter hits max health every 5s while Cell Division blobs heal him

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a back-and-forth: his blob sustain keeps him competitive in prolonged trades, but your Heat management and Electro-Harpoon kit outpaces his damage.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 swing back and forth: Unstable Matter is a 5-second max-health hit inside 350 range, so length favours him — burst and leave rather than brawl.

edits.before: The whole mid-lane phase is about Elastic Slingshot tracking. When it is down, run your full pattern — Q through him at 50+ Heat, double-E to prevent disengage, and back off before you Overheat. When it is up, respect it: give him nothing, stay near terrain you can use for cover, and bait the cast so you can W-shield through the landing CC. At level 6 your Equalizer fundamentally outvalues his ultimate in the lane — when he uses his R to engage, your R punishes every champion who followed him in. If you are ahead, freeze and starve him; his blob sustain only matters if trades go long and grinding.
edits.after: The whole mid-lane phase is Elastic Slingshot tracking, and it is 21 seconds at rank 1 — the longest window either of you gets. When it is down, run your full pattern: Q through him at 50+ Heat, double-E to deny the disengage, and back off before you Overheat. When it is up, give him nothing, stay near terrain you can use for cover, and bait the cast so you can W-shield through the landing. At level 6 your Equalizer outvalues Let's Bounce, 120 seconds at rank 1 — when he bounces in to engage, your R punishes every champion who followed him. If you are ahead, freeze and starve him; his blob sustain only matters if trades go long and grinding.

edits.before: Late game this is a genuine tossup — Zac builds into a teamfight tank that your percent-health burn loves, but Equalizer does most of your work without you needing to be anywhere near him. Your job is to drop the wall across his slingshot landing zone in every big fight so his engage costs his team dearly. Do not try to 1v1 him if he has Knight's Vow or a Locket-wielding support nearby; his passive blob sustain can be nearly unkillable in extended fights. Pivot to cross-map Equalizer plays and let your team follow his CC-reliant dive with your AoE punishment.
edits.after: Late game this is a genuine tossup — Zac builds into a teamfight tank that your percent-health burn loves, but Equalizer does most of your work without you needing to be anywhere near him. Your job is to drop the wall across his slingshot landing zone in every big fight so his engage costs his team dearly. Do not 1v1 him with a Knight's Vow or Locket support nearby, and check Cell Division before you commit: lethal damage splits him into four bloblets and he revives from whatever survives, on a five-minute cooldown. Pivot to cross-map Equalizer plays and let your team follow his dive with your AoE punishment.

notes: Both packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES — 'Drop Equalizer' and 'Land Elastic Slingshot' are correct names and were left alone. The real naming defect the scanner missed was wants.foe[0] attributing crowd control to W: Unstable Matter is a max-health damage pulse, not CC. DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN: Zac's Elastic Slingshot carries a 'grounding' derived flag, but Riot's description ('attaches his arms to the ground and stretches back, launching himself forward') contains no grounding effect, so I made no grounding claim. The _missing-interactions 'knockup-enabler' entry pairs Zac's Q and E against Rumble's Scrap Shield, but Scrap Shield's knockup and terrain flags are tooltip misfires — Riot's text is shield plus move speed only — so I wrote no displacement-race line and nothing implying Scrap Shield or The Equalizer blocks the slingshot. The Equalizer slows, it does not wall a dash.
